providers.title: Randomness does not raise the value of a projection game
providers.scope: If the players of a projection game use random numbers independent of the edge, their probability of winning is at most the value of the game.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A gap for formulas with three different variables per clause
providers.scope: Assuming a PCP theorem with perfect completeness for constraint systems of bounded arity: there are gamma_0 > 0 and a polynomial-time map to 3-CNF formulas with three different variables per clause that preserves satisfiability and makes every assignment violate a fraction gamma_0 of the clauses in the unsatisfiable case.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The value of the clause-variable game
providers.scope: For a 3-CNF formula Psi the clause-variable game has value 1 if Psi is satisfiable, and at most 1 - gamma/3 if every assignment violates a fraction gamma of the clauses.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The base game: a projection game with perfect completeness and small soundness
providers.scope: Assuming the PCP theorem with perfect completeness and parallel repetition for projection games: for every sigma > 0 a polynomial-time map from formulas to projection games with answer sets of sizes 7^t and 2^t, of value 1 for satisfiable formulas and at most sigma otherwise.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sets of matrices over F_2 that are often preserved by a rank-one step
providers.scope: Assuming the expansion theorem for Grassmann graphs (GE): a set S of l x m matrices over F_2 with P(M + a h^T in S) >= eta for M uniform in S has density at least alpha in a slice with at most r row combinations and r column values; alpha, r depend only on eta (l and m large).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Projection of a slice of matrices to a subset of the columns
providers.scope: For a slice of matrices on H + D, its image on H is a slice with the same row combinations and at most as many column values, and all fibres of the projection have the same size.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Inverse theorem for partial tables on matrices over F_2
providers.scope: Assuming (GE): if a partial table f on K tensor H satisfies P(f(M) = f(M + ah) defined) >= eta, some value fills a fraction alpha of a slice with at most r row combinations and r column values; alpha, r, l_0 depend only on eta, not on dim H or on the number of values.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Many good row fibres
providers.scope: Assuming (GE): under the hypothesis of the inverse theorem with eta, a uniform matrix lies in a good row fibre for some row map with probability at least eta/4, and for a uniform row map with probability at least (eta/4) 2^(-r l).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The function spaces on the tree
providers.scope: The spaces H_D (all functions at a leaf; at an inner node the sum of the spans of products of two functions of each child) contain 1, satisfy H_C^2 in H_D for every proper descendant C of D, and are preserved by the pull-back along the projections of the base game.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shared keys
providers.scope: A function on the answers of a mixed family of base questions and its composition with the projection from the full family have the same key (the same typed reduced domain and partition) and the same restored values.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Constraints of the new game have at most two preimages
providers.scope: The constraint of (E, M, D, a), which forgets the component along a of the value at the node D, is a map from the labels of the left key onto the labels of the right key with at most two preimages of every label.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Perfect completeness of the new game
providers.scope: If the formula is satisfiable, one labeling of all keys satisfies every constraint, for all choices of the parameters; so every game supported on these constraints has value 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Joint folding
providers.scope: Adding to a row of the array at a node D a constant and products of rows of arrays at proper descendants keeps the key of the joint function, and for every label the restored value of that row changes by the same constant and the same products of restored values.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The functional of a response on products of displayed rows
providers.scope: For a label with restored values y_C there is exactly one functional on the span of 1 and of the products of the rows at given proper descendants with value 1 at 1 and (y_C)_u (y_C)_v at the products; every extension to H_D has the matrices y_C y_C^T, of rank at most one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Buckets and steps of rank one
providers.scope: If the buckets h_v, v nonzero in K, are independent and uniform in H, then M = sum v tensor h_v is uniform in K tensor H, and resampling the bucket of a nonzero a replaces M by M + a tensor h with h uniform and independent of M and a.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The game of the reduction before the completion of the alphabets
providers.scope: The tests (base questions at the leaves, a random path with recursive samples, uniform arrays off the path, a constraint at a random level of the path) define a projection game with at most two preimages of every label and value 1 for a satisfiable formula.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
